unresolved_findings.judge_assessment: Stands, as a nit. Reproduced at 93ced45 with my own probe because the reviewer's probes/ directory is not in this sandbox. I replaced to_dict with `overdue = self.is_overdue(today); return {**asdict(self), "overdue": overdue}`. Result: pytest 39 passed, local-all 10/0, rollover-local passed. A race probe (create past-due todo, to_dict, against a thread spinning complete()) shows 110 torn in 20000, e.g. done=true with overdue=true. A second hook test that patches Todo.is_overdue to call complete(1) after the original passes at head and fails on this mutant. Head itself is correct: 0 torn in 20000. The implementer has not responded, because this is new in the reviewer's round 2. It is a gap in regression protection against a hypothetical refactor, not a defect in the change, so it does not block. Optional follow-up: parametrize test_post_response_stays_consistent_when_completed_while_it_is_built over the is_overdue hook point.

Withdrawal confirmed by execution. Refutation condition (a) is met literally: at head the race probe gives 0 torn in 20000. With the round-1 to_dict (`{**asdict(self), 'overdue': self.is_overdue(today)}`) it gives 70 torn in 20000, and test_post_response_stays_consistent_when_completed_while_it_is_built fails (1 failed, 38 passed). The reason for the withdrawal is stated.

At 5fd5533, 7a5bfd4 and e563e95, '2026-11-30T00:00:00', 0, 1700000000 and '2027-02-29' all give 422 with 0 todos stored. The reason is stated and checks out.

residual_risks: F-5 (nit, open): the F-1 regression test catches only one read order. An overdue-first to_dict without a snapshot passes the whole plan and re-opens a done/overdue race (110/20000 torn in my probe). Human decision: accept it, or ask for the second hook test as a follow-up.

Preview evidence is not a deployed environment: test_results.json shows the 9 'preview' e2e entries exit 0 against an orchestrator-started local instance (mode local, http://127.0.0.1:54991). preview.yml deploys nothing, per the owner. The reviewer could not reach that instance, so this rests on the orchestrator's authoritative run.

AC-10 (overdue flips at a date rollover with no write) has no live evidence, by owner decision. It is proven only with a patched clock: test_overdue_flips_when_the_date_advances_without_a_write and rollover-local, both passing.
The overdue cutoff is UTC midnight for every user (owner-confirmed, human_comments.md (3)). Users in, for example, UTC-8 see todos go overdue at 16:00 local time on their due date.

test_today_utc_is_the_utc_date_not_the_host_date patches app.storage.datetime and pins the exact datetime.now(timezone.utc) call. An equivalent but differently written UTC implementation would fail it. That body is what spec.interfaces prescribes, so this is acceptable coupling.

The reviewer measured (I did not re-measure) that the per-todo replace() copy inside list_dicts runs under the store lock and adds roughly 50-100% lock hold time at 10k-50k todos. The spec sets no performance budget, and this in-memory sample is not expected to hold that many todos.
local-all picks its fake host TZ once at start, so a run that crosses 12:00 or 00:00 UTC loses its ability to catch a host-date mutant for that run. It cannot cause a false failure.

Review record hygiene: findings.json renumbers findings across rounds (the F-2 claim appears twice, as F-2 and F-3; round-1 F-3 is now F-4; checks_performed calls the new nit F-4, while the findings array calls it F-5). checks_performed also concatenates two round-2 passes with different figures (118/1007 vs 88/633). There is no code impact, but a later audit should not rely on the ids.
summary_for_human:
What changed: POST /todos takes an optional due_date (null, or a real YYYY-MM-DD date; anything else gets 422 and nothing is stored). Every todo response gains due_date and a derived overdue flag (open AND due_date strictly before the current UTC date), and the new GET /todos/overdue returns exactly the overdue todos in id order. 5 files change, all inside allowed_paths: app/storage.py (+today_utc, Todo.is_overdue/to_dict, TodoStore.list_dicts), app/main.py (TodoIn.due_date + validator, new route), README.md, tests/test_overdue.py (36 tests), tests/e2e_overdue.py.

Contested and settled (I re-ran each on a clean clone of 93ced45): F-1, a torn done/overdue pair in POST responses under a concurrent complete(): fixed with a snapshot in to_dict. My race probe gives 0 torn in 20000 at head and 70 with the round-1 to_dict, and the new regression test fails on the round-1 code. F-2, today_utc() could use the host date undetected: fixed. With TZ=UTC, the mutants date.today(), datetime.now().date() and datetime.now().astimezone().date() each fail test_today_utc_is_the_utc_date_not_the_host_date and 3 local-all checks. Old F-3, an intermediate commit that stored malformed dates: the history was rebuilt, d33b244 is not an ancestor of HEAD, and every remaining commit gives 422 for the datetime and integer values. All 8 deterministic checks pass.

Still open (nit, non-blocking, reproduced): F-5. The F-1 regression test only catches the asdict-first read order. Rewriting to_dict as `overdue = self.is_overdue(today); return {**asdict(self), ...}` passes all 39 pytest tests, local-all and rollover-local, yet my probe shows 110 torn responses in 20000. Decide whether to accept this or ask for the 10-line second hook (patch Todo.is_overdue) as a follow-up.

Evidence for the criteria: AC-1..AC-9 each have a named test in tests/test_overdue.py, a local-all check and an orchestrator e2e run (test_results.json, 9/9 exit 0). AC-10 rests on test_overdue_flips_when_the_date_advances_without_a_write plus rollover-local. AC-11: 39 passed, with tests/test_todos.py unchanged. AC-12/13: static plan commands exit 0. Know this about the 'preview': it was an orchestrator-started local instance (mode local, 127.0.0.1:54991, not a deployed environment), and the reviewer could not reach it.

Read first: app/storage.py (to_dict snapshot and list_dicts under the lock), then the TodoIn validator in app/main.py, then tests/test_overdue.py tests test_post_response_stays_consistent_when_completed_while_it_is_built and test_today_utc_is_the_utc_date_not_the_host_date.
